body:
Problem:
User-input payloads (`getchar`/`input`) to 'operatorfunc' and `:omap` motion (e.g. vim-sneak `dz{target}/cz{target}`), reaches `CmdAtom.keys` but not redo (dot-repeat).

This means historically, plugins have done creative things to support redo (vim-repeat, "caching" (e.g. mini.surround, mini.operators), dynamic expr-mappings, …). Meanwhile, multicursor cascade does NOT work with such "creative" solutions: it _expects_ plugins to passively behave (e.g., wait for `getchar` input as usual) during replay.

Solution:
- For 'operatorfunc': append the payload after `restore_redobuff()`.
- For `:omap` motion: append the payload when the op is captured.

Guidance for plugins: "re-read, don't cache". Dot-repeat and multicursor-cascade will "just work".

Tradeoff: the creative plugins will need to adapt.

fix #41657
fix https://github.com/justinmk/vim-sneak/issues/329

comment_regular_data.body:
> Solution:
> 
> * For 'operatorfunc': append the payload after `restore_redobuff()`.
> 
> * For `:omap` motion: append the payload when the op is captured.
> 
> Guidance for plugins: "re-read, don't cache". Dot-repeat and multicursor-cascade will "just work".
> 
> Tradeoff: the creative plugins will need to adapt.

That is a very bad trade-off: a breaking change that essentially punishes plugins that provide out-of-the-box dot-repeat, in favor of plugins that didn't bother to do it and by obfuscation resolving #41657 (which has another solution of using `CmdAtom.lhs` instead of `CmdAtom.keys`, without obviously stated downsides).

This would be a problem for any sort of labelled jump, where the previous user input becomes irrelevant on dot-repeat. You would either want to either re-prompt or have some kind of consistent fallback behavior.

> This would be a problem for any sort of labelled jump, where the previous user input becomes irrelevant on dot-repeat.

Example? It works with vim-sneak. If the labels are deterministic then it should work. How else is the plugin deciding what to repeat?

> > This would be a problem for any sort of labelled jump, where the previous user input becomes irrelevant on dot-repeat.
> 
> Example? It works with vim-sneak. If the labels are deterministic then it should work. How else is the plugin deciding what to repeat?

Example is if plugin *actually wants* to re-ask for the user input on dot-repeat, which makes more sense for "labeled jump" kind of plugins. So like `d` - `<init jump>` - `<user input for label>` deletes until the selected user label; then later `.` will show and re-ask until what jump label to delete and repeat the delete. With automatically forcing the same user input on `.` this would not be possible (at least not without hacks).

Concrete examples are at least 'mini.jump2d', 'folke/flash.nvim', and probably some other similar "labelled jump" plugins.

> Example is if plugin _actually wants_ to re-ask for the user input on dot-repeat, which makes more sense for "labeled jump" kind of plugins. So like `d` - `<init jump>` - `<user input for label>` deletes until the selected user label; then later `.` will show and re-ask until what jump label to delete and repeat the delete

That is arbitrarily changing the purpose of dot-repeat.

> That is arbitrarily changing the purpose of dot-repeat.

Of course it is not. Pressing `dot` *will* repeat the last edit/operator, but on the new re-computed motion/range. In this case re-computation includes asking a user for the target, in other cases it doesn't.

> In this case re-computation includes asking a user for the target,

And how is that supposed to work for multicursor?

> > In this case re-computation includes asking a user for the target,
> 
> And how is that supposed to work for multicursor?

Ideally - re-asking for each cursor. Otherwise they all will jump to the same spot (or worse - unpredictable spots if edits are made) which is questionably useful. This functionality is rarely a "relative" type of jump ("third occurrence of letter `e`"), but "absolute" type of jump ("*this exact* letter `e` in this *this exact* window").

Also not having it work for multicursor, while still working for dot-repeat is a totally fine use case. Making it work in multicursor will probably be doable on plugin side, but will require much more exported inspection API for multicursor, like `nvim_mcursor_get()` which returns info about multicursor session id, currently cascading multicursor id, etc.

> In this case re-computation includes asking a user for the target, in other cases it doesn't.

That is arbitrary, and contrary to the purpose of dot-repeat. That is a plugin-specific use-case ("I want to repeat only part of the last operation"), not dot-repeat.

That "worked" accidentally because Vim didn't capture `getchar` input in dot-repeat. But plugins use `getchar` for various purposes because that is the *only option they have*. For example, f/t plugins.

As a compromise, allowing the dot-repeat register to be modified by plugins (`setrepeat()`) would serve your use-case, while the common case to "just work".

> This functionality is rarely a "relative" type of jump ("third occurrence of letter `e`"), but "absolute" type of jump ("_this exact_ letter `e` in this _this exact_ window").

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41960#issuecomment-5721596332 is an example that wants best-effort repeat of jumps. Though a plugin is not involved there, but the general idea is the same.

> > In this case re-computation includes asking a user for the target, in other cases it doesn't.
> 
> That is arbitrary, and contrary to the purpose of dot-repeat. That is a plugin-specific use-case ("I want to repeat only part of the last operation"), not dot-repeat.

This is turning into semantics debate, which we clearly don't agree on.

Both of the following are valid cases for dot repeat actions: 1) "delete from here till the next `e`; 2) "delete from here till the label provided by the user". First pre-computes the target, second delegates on each repeat. First will be possible after this PR *if* plugins update accordingly (which is already bad), the second will be problematic to have (if at all) and will require more complex changes.

---

In the end of the day, plugins that won't adapt to this PR will have broken dot-repeat and multicursor behavior. Without this PR they will have broken only multicursor behavior. Both cases require adaptation to how user input is consumed. Both cases are possible (especially if `vim.api.nvim__mcursor_cascading()` is properly exported for the second case). But only one of them breaks existing functionality and *forces* plugins to update.

> plugins that won't adapt to this PR will have broken dot-repeat

Lots of plugins have broken dot-repeat in the current state, because they are "doing things wrong" (i.e. not working-around Vim/Nvim limitations).

> Without this PR they will have broken only multicursor behavior.
>
> ... Both cases are possible (especially if `vim.api.nvim__mcursor_cascading()` is properly exported for the second case).

Ok, either https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41657 is not a release blocker, *or* `nvim_get_mode().cascading` can be coupled with this PR.

> > Without this PR they will have broken only multicursor behavior.
> > ... Both cases are possible (especially if `vim.api.nvim__mcursor_cascading()` is properly exported for the second case).
> 
> Ok, either #41657 is not a release blocker, _or_ `nvim_get_mode().cascading` can be coupled with this PR.

*Or* `nvim_get_mode().cascading` can be its own thing without being tied to this PR. It is useful by itself, including to some built-in functionality. Although I'd think a more forward thinking approach would be a dedicated `nvim_mcursor_get()`, which can be extended to provide more state info about multicursor.

Also (and I think I'll ask one last time) using `CmdAtom.lhs` instead of `CmdAtom.keys` is the possibility. There is no obviously stated counter-example (when using `lhs` makes it not work, but `keys` magically does).

> a more forward thinking approach would be a dedicated `nvim_mcursor_get()`, which can be extended to provide more state info about multicursor.

Sure, but API is not a priority right now. Need to get the basic UX settled first.

> There is no obviously stated counter-example (when using `lhs` makes it not work, but `keys` magically does).

Replied at https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41657#issuecomment-5817223339 so the discussion lives in the issue tracker.
